svg.aria-label: How to write ن، ت، ث: 3 letters, ن, ت, ث, one after another
svg.title: Writing ن، ت، ث
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ن, ت, ث (arabic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ن: Waraqa Institute, The Letter Noon in Arabic — Writing Noon: The Bowl Shape and Its Single Dot, Step 4 (accessed 2026-08-21) <https://www.waraqaweb.com/lessons/letter-noon-in-arabic>; ت: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ب ت ث, independent Baa at 00:02–00:04 and Taa at 00:00–00:01 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023) <https://opentext.uoregon.edu/introarabic/chapter/two-way-connectors-%D8%A8-%D8%AA-%D8%AB-%D9%86-%D9%8A/>; ث: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: ب ت ث, independent Thaa demonstration (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023) <https://opentext.uoregon.edu/introarabic/chapter/two-way-connectors-%D8%A8-%D8%AA-%D8%AB-%D9%86-%D9%8A/>. Source notes on variation: ن: The cited beginner lesson explicitly orders isolated ن body-first: begin at the curve's top right, sweep down and around in one smooth motion through the deep below-baseline bowl, then add the single centred upper dot last. It distinguishes this deep isolated/final bowl from the shallow forms of ب, ت, and ث and separately identifies the initial/medial form as a small tooth. The same lesson identifies Noon as a two-way connector. This two-stroke, one-lift independent learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline while retaining Arabic-scoped provenance separately from the existing Persian and Urdu records for the same Unicode glyph. ت: The page's Baa demonstration verifies the shared independent bowl from its upper-right tip continuously right-to-left to the turned-up left tip. The Taa demonstration opens on that complete bowl, places the left dot above at 00:00.45–00:00.70, then lifts again and places the right dot at 00:00.75–00:01.00. Because the Taa clip does not redraw the bowl, this learner path uses the separately demonstrated Arabic Baa body rather than inferring its direction from a still. The adjacent lesson identifies taa as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. The path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline; its Arabic provenance remains separate from the Persian record for the same Unicode glyph. ث: The page's dedicated Thaa video demonstrates independent ث body-first. It sweeps the shared shallow bowl from the upper-right tip continuously right-to-left to the turned-up left tip, then adds the three upper dots as separate marks in the visible two-lower-and-one-centred-upper arrangement. This learner path places those dots lower-left, lower-right, then centred upper, for four pen-down runs separated by three lifts. The adjacent lesson identifies thaa as a two-way connector, gives its th sound, and prints its contextual shapes. The path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline; its Arabic provenance remains separate from any cross-script reuse of the shared bowl geometry.
